title: Fresh-seed review (13) of c44's CIPS seasons negative: replicated; with lo 0.25 the bodies never die (4-5 throughout), and a 50 t total famine every 2000 t shrinks every body to a diffuse core (occupancy 0.09 -> 0.001-0.003) from which all regrow in place (8 bodies before and after each later famine), so no selective death
summary: Ran the finding's world.py unchanged on seed 13 (128^2, 200 frames, t=20000) with seasons from t=6000, period 2000: (a) season_lo 0.25, frac 0.5; (b) season_lo 0, frac 0.025 (50 t total famine). (a): 4 bodies before the seasons, 4-5 after, 0 deaths, 3 persistent splits. (b): at every famine the body count by labkit's segmentation drops to 0-3 and occupancy to 0.001-0.003, and within ~500 t the same bodies are back at the same sites (pulse025/series.txt: 8, 8, 8 between famines from t=10500 to t=19500; sheet t=20000 is inside a famine and shows the cores). Early on, two famines are followed by divisions of elongated bodies (4 -> 8 by t~10500), after which the count stays at 8. labkit counts 36 nucleations in (b) because shrunken cores fall below the threshold and regrow; they are not new bodies.

observations.D: negative replicated: lo25/series.txt 4-5 bodies after t=6000, 0 deaths; pulse025/series.txt every famine drops occupancy to 0.001-0.003 and every body regrows at its site (8 before and after each famine from t=10500), pulse025/seed13/sheet.png t=20000 (cores during a famine)

seeds_run.result: replicates both arms: no deaths at lo 0.25; total 50 t famines shrink all bodies to cores that regrow in place

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, two of the four arms (lo 0.5 and the 30 t famine not re-run). After the first famines the bodies divided (4 -> 8), so famines may trigger division once, which the finding does not mention; whether that recurs in a larger box is untested.
